references.text: Hagar gives God a name after seeing Him, a parallel to Jacob naming the place Peniel after seeing God face to face.
God appears to Jacob in a dream at Bethel, which is an earlier meeting between God and Jacob before the event at Peniel.
God appears again to Jacob after Peniel at Bethel, where God blesses Jacob and confirms his name change.
The elders of Israel saw God and ate and drank – they survived the encounter with God, just as Jacob survived seeing God face to face.
Moses' prayer to see God's glory, and God's answer that no one can see His face and live, provides an important contrast to Jacob's experience at Peniel.
Moses knew the Lord face to face – a parallel to Jacob's statement of having seen God face to face.
Gideon fears for his life after seeing the angel of the Lord face to face, which mirrors Jacob's fear and surprise at surviving after seeing God.
Manoah fears for his life after seeing God, a parallel to Jacob's surprise at having seen God face to face and yet survived.
Verse 33:10 gives the theological interpretation of the 'face to face' experience in 32:31 by linking the reunion with Esau directly to God's grace.
Thematic parallel between two patriarchs who name places after a life-saving revelation where they 'see' God.
